title: Musinsa Accelerates Greater China Push, to Open 5th China Store in Shenzhen
snippet: Musinsa is accelerating its Greater China expansion, opening a fifth China store in Shenzhen in September while foreign sales and global store transactions
extractedText: Musinsa Accelerates Greater China Push, to Open 5th China Store in ShenzhenStore to Open in Shenzhen in September, Expanding into Southern ChinaFinance|Published 2026.07.12. 11:57:19|By Kim Yeon-ha|Summary|SaveAAA'Musinsa Standard Hangzhou Hanglong Plaza Store.' Photo courtesy of MusinsaMusinsa is accelerating the expansion of its overseas brick-and-mortar stores as it strengthens its global market push. From late last year through the first half of this year, the company opened four new stores in China, and in the second half it plans to open a Musinsa Standard store in Shenzhen, China. It has also announced plans to open 15 stores in Taiwan over the next five years, part of a concentrated push into the Greater China region.According to the fashion industry on the 12th, Musinsa will open a Musinsa Standard offline store in September in Shenzhen, known as China's Silicon Valley. After focusing on the eastern coastal cities of Shanghai and Hangzhou, the company is now expanding into the southern region. Shenzhen, along with Beijing and Shanghai, is one of China's representative first-tier cities, with an economy ranking third to fourth in gross domestic product (GDP) among all Chinese cities.Musinsa opened its first overseas store, "Musinsa Standard Shanghai Huaihai Baisheng," in Shanghai in January this year, followed in succession by "Musinsa Standard Shanghai Shinsegae Xinhuan Center" in March, and "Musinsa Standard Shanghai Xinlu 600 YOUNG" and "Musinsa Standard Hangzhou Hanglong Plaza" in April.As a result of these new store openings, transaction volume at Musinsa Standard's China stores in the second quarter of this year grew more than threefold compared with the first quarter. In addition, as offline popularity spread online, Musinsa Standard's second-quarter transaction volume on Tmall, China's largest online shopping mall, also increased 27%."In the second half, we will open a store in Shenzhen as well and expand our business into the southern China consumer market," a Musinsa official said. "We plan to begin expanding our global infrastructure in earnest so that consumers around the world, including in Southeast Asia, can experience Musinsa Standard both online and offline."Musinsa Standard is also growing its standing as a global fashion brand by targeting foreign tourists visiting Korea. In the first half of this year, sales to foreigners at its domestic offline stores rose 67% from a year earlier. In particular, at five foreigner-focused stores in Gangnam, Myeongdong, Seongsu, Hannam, and Hongdae, which draw many foreign tourists, foreign purchases accounted for an average of 54%, surpassing half.The company is also employing a strategy to turn foreign tourists who visit its domestic stores into long-term customers. A representative example is running integrated online-offline promotions, such as offering discount coupons to customers who sign up for the Musinsa Global Store at major stores with high foreign visitor rates. The company has built a structure in which offline stores function as points of contact with global customers, connecting them so they make repeat purchases online even after returning to their home countries.As this strategy paid off, transaction volume for Musinsa Standard within the Musinsa Global Store in the first half of this year increased 236% from a year earlier. Driven by Musinsa Standard's success, the Global Store's monthly transaction volume in June also surpassed 21 billion won, reaching a record monthly high since the Global Store's launch."Musinsa Standard is expanding its growth axis beyond 'inbound,' which absorbs the shopping demand of foreign tourists visiting Korea, to 'outbound,' which directly targets local consumers overseas," a Musinsa official emphasized.#Musinsa#MusinsaStandard#KoreanFashion#ChinaMarket#Shenzhen#RetailExpansion#KfashionOriginal reporting by Kim Yeon-ha for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
